claims.statement: The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation provides for a methodology to identify packaging material composition using standardised, open digital-marking technologies.
The Regulation applies from August 2026 but implementing details can continue to affect data requirements.

contrary_evidence: The mandated technologies are intended to be open, which can reduce software lock-in and commoditise simple record display.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated: sign a few packaging converters whose records automatically reach many brand customers; use the founder's FMCG domain understanding without employer data.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: map 1,000 SKUs in year 1, reach 4 million PLN ARR by year 4, build 4 million PLN founder equity and retained cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-9.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-4 hours per day with converter onboarding templates and external verification.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 70%-90% gross margin after initial data mapping, verification and support.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 9-18 months after the first converter portfolio goes live.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated commercial figures, including capital_required_pln: 40-120 PLN per active SKU per month, with 5,000-25,000 PLN converter onboarding.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: records recur while SKUs remain active and update on material changes; churn is unknown.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-converter schemas, change histories and validation exceptions make onboarding faster and evidence more trusted
fingerprint.customer: Packaging converters and EU FMCG brands maintaining packaging material records
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Converters originate the record and distribute it downstream with every customer specification
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Versioned packaging composition evidence with stable identifiers and system integrations
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A converter or brand pays for each active governed record and onboarding
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A SKU launches or its packaging material, component or supplier changes

founder_fit: Uses FMCG context without requiring employer information.
Strong fit for data modelling and automation.
Structural converter distribution limits outbound sales.
risks: Open standards make the basic product easy to copy.
Incorrect source data exposes customers to mislabelling.
Employer-conflict and confidentiality boundaries must be strict.

structure.control_point: Converter distribution agreements and contractual rights to normalise, version and serve packaging-composition evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Converters must supply accurate component data, brands must accept the evidence record and the service must align with final EU methods

thesis: Contract packaging converters to maintain verified material bill-of-material records at the source, issue stable evidence identifiers and push updates into FMCG customer workflows. The product is a governed evidence rail with converter-originated data rights and change history, not a generic PPWR compliance dashboard.
title: Packaging Composition Evidence Rail
uncertainties: Who pays: converter, brand or producer-responsibility organisation
Willingness to grant durable evidence-serving rights
